items.title: RoboMIND's humanoid dataset clears 20 million downloads
items.summary: The Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics says its open-sourced RoboMIND dataset — 300,000-plus dual-arm manipulation trajectories spanning more than 700 real-world tasks on 40 robot configurations — has doubled its download count in a month. The figure is self-reported, and as humanoid.guide notes, downloads aren't deployed models or completed training runs.

items.title: ROBOTIS opens a sim-to-real gym for student humanoids
items.summary: The Korean firm's Open Humanoid GYM packs simulation, motion development and AI training layers into an open-source program built around its AI Sapiens K1 platform, with students moving full-body behaviors from simulator to physical robot over a one-month program, according to a report cited by humanoid.guide. Key implementation details remain unspecified, and the outlet frames it for now as an educational humanoid test bed.

items.title: NVIDIA snaps up Hugging Face for $12.9 billion
items.summary: The chipmaker has agreed to buy the open AI development platform that also houses LeRobot, the open-source library for robot datasets, models and policies. NVIDIA says Hugging Face will remain open to the entire AI ecosystem — and that NVIDIA compute will not be required to build or deploy on it.

items.title: Visko's Orbis streams interactive worlds by the hour
items.summary: The Sunnyvale startup's first 'live model' generates frame by frame the way an LLM predicts tokens – streaming 4K video at 24 fps, taking prompt changes mid-generation and sustaining hour-scale runs without drift, according to founder Qing Yin. Visko pitches Orbis for robotics training and simulation, opened public access at launch and closed a $10 million pre-seed led by Llama Ventures.

items.title: Kinetic Blocks puts robot training data up for sale
items.summary: The Oslo startup's new marketplace lists egocentric video, teleoperation recordings and robot execution data with chain-of-custody documentation and a quality grade, and buyers walk away with a commercial licence at checkout, according to the company. It opens September 1 as a gated beta, with sellers and buyers approved individually.

items.title: Skild's S1 learns a 10-minute chore from one video
items.summary: Skild AI says its flagship S1 foundation model picks up long-horizon tasks like repotting a plant or cooking pancakes from a single human video added to its prompt, and that the same 'omni-bodied' brain runs quadrupeds, static arms and humanoids alike. CEO Deepak Pathak tells The Robot Report that humanoid performance is the next focus – and that robotics still hasn't hit its ChatGPT moment.

items.title: Sanctuary skips the humanoid and ships the brain
items.summary: Carbon, the control system Sanctuary developed alongside its Phoenix humanoid, handled live-conveyor wire insertion at a global Tier 1 automotive supplier – 313 trials, a 99.5% success rate, 2.54 seconds a cycle, according to the company. Sanctuary pitches the system as Physical AI for currently available industrial robots with off-the-shelf end effectors; for now it's a proof of concept, not a production deployment.

items.title: EXL scoops up physical-AI data trainer iMerit
items.summary: ExlService Holdings has completed its purchase of iMerit, the San Jose firm whose annotation workforce and Ango Hub platform prepare multimodal training, evaluation and reinforcement-learning data for robotics and autonomous mobility. Founder Radha Basu stays on to run the unit inside EXL, which says the deal connects parts of the AI lifecycle that have often been managed separately.

items.title: Hugging Face's $399 Microduck opens up physical AI
items.summary: The 25 cm robot waddles, roller-skates and rights itself after falls, and its simulation, SDK and reinforcement-learning stack are open source, so behaviors trained in sim run straight on the hardware, according to Hugging Face. CEO Clem Delangue pitches it as the start of affordable open robots that democratize physical AI and world models, with shipping due before Christmas.

items.title: NSF backs a $30M center for human-robot co-adaptation
items.summary: The U.S. National Science Foundation is putting $90 million into three new Science and Technology Centers, and the robotics one — the Center for Human and Robot Co-Adaptation at the University of Texas at Austin — gets $30 million over five years to study how people and robots with embodied intelligence adapt to one another as service and assistive robots spread through homes, hospitals and workplaces. Apptronik, Google DeepMind and NVIDIA are among the center's industry partners, according to the university.

items.title: Perceptron's Isaac 0.5 gives factory robots an open-weight eye
items.summary: Perceptron, founded by two former Meta AI researchers, has released Isaac 0.5, an open-weight vision model built to let industrial robots perceive, reason and act — rejecting what the founders call a false choice between heavyweight generalist models and narrow perception-only systems. It was trained on a million hours of video, from egocentric footage to human demonstrations, according to the company.

items.title: Robot brains are still in their GPT-2 era, builders say
items.summary: Reporting from Actuate — a robotics conference that has tripled in size since 2023, drawing 1,500 attendees according to organizer Foxglove — TechCrunch finds robot hardware outrunning the models that control it, with physical AI sitting in its 'GPT-2 era', as Antioch founder Harry Mellsop puts it. Wayve CEO Alex Kendall reckons manipulation robotics today is roughly where self-driving was five years ago.

items.title: NVIDIA's Jetson Orin Nano 2 doubles the entry-level robot brain
items.summary: The 78-TOPS module delivers twice the inference performance of its predecessor and, according to NVIDIA, lets robots run frontier LLMs and vision-language models directly on the edge. It is slated for the first half of 2027, with a 15-watt mode that matches the outgoing board's peak output on 40% less power.

items.title: General Intuition courts a $6B valuation to crack robotics
items.summary: The Medal spinout, which trains action models on hundreds of millions of hours of gameplay footage, is raising an oversubscribed round at a $6 billion pre-money valuation — up from $2.3 billion in June — with Valor Equity Partners, Point72 Ventures and Seven Seven Six joining, according to TechCrunch. The new money is earmarked for compute and for extending its general model to robotic embodiments.

items.title: Generalist stacks another $200M onto its Series B
items.summary: Two months after its $400 million June round, the robot-brains developer has added roughly $200 million more led by 8VC, with NVIDIA, Bezos Expeditions and Fei-Fei Li among the backers, according to an SEC filing reported by Axios. TechCrunch says the extension lifts Generalist's Series B to $600 million in total.

items.title: Scaling robots is a staffing problem, HireArt argues
items.summary: The limiting factor in real-world robot deployments is rarely the robot but the workforce that operates, maintains and adapts it, argues HireArt co-founder Christopher Bower in The Robot Report. He describes a new layer of roles sitting between engineering and operations — teleoperators, data capture specialists, QA validators and field technicians.

items.title: NVIDIA and Berkeley give robot touch its own reflex loop
items.summary: T-Rex pairs a slower vision-based planner with a fast tactile expert that corrects grips in real time — processing four touch updates for every vision update to catch contact events cameras miss, like a USB connector settling into its port. The open-source release includes 50 hours of robot play data across roughly 5,500 episodes from a 22-degree-of-freedom tactile hand — the largest released tactile dataset to date, according to the collaborators, though no benchmark scores accompany the launch.

items.title: Generalist claims one-shot task learning with GEN-1.5
items.summary: Generalist says its new GEN-1.5 system can pick up a physical task from a single demonstration in a few seconds and then generalize what it was shown, crediting pretraining on physical data at scale. The announcement names no benchmarks, success rates or hardware, humanoid.guide notes, so the claim can't be assessed yet.

items.title: NVIDIA's platform sits inside 80% of the world's humanoids
items.summary: More than 80% of humanoid robots worldwide are estimated to use NVIDIA's robotics platform — its chips, GR00T foundation models and training environments — according to ABI Research data cited by Chosun. humanoid.guide notes the figure blends two very different dependencies: robots running NVIDIA hardware and those trained with its software.

items.title: Generalist's data recipe: human hours, robot minutes
items.summary: Generalist told The Robot Report it builds robot manipulation skills from 2–80 hours of human demonstration data per task, then refines them with as little as 4–80 minutes of robot-collected footage. According to the company, the models it has run on Universal Robots and Flexiv cobot arms weren't programmed for error recovery — they learned it from other interactions in its dataset.

items.title: Newton 1.5 wires joint control into GPU-scale robot sims
items.summary: The open-source Newton simulation project's v1.5.0 release introduces experimental vectorized joint control with impedance controllers for GPU-scale robot batches, plus multi-world simulation tools and steadier contact modeling. Humanoid benchmark workloads initialize 11–24% faster, according to the release notes.

items.title: Robots are learning in silent worlds, Treble warns
items.summary: Humanoids will be judged less by how they move than by how they communicate, argues Treble Technologies co-founder Gunnar Pétur Hauksson — yet the environments robots train in are overwhelmingly visual and, for the most part, silent. The Icelandic firm's simulation platform generates physically accurate acoustic training data with a low sim-to-real gap and is already used by leading technology companies, according to Treble.

items.title: DEF CON's robot hacks become a free Isaac Sim test suite
items.summary: Trend Micro subsidiary VicOne has released a free Radeis extension for NVIDIA Isaac Sim that lets developers replay adversarial visual prompts, malicious inputs and sensor manipulation attacks against their own robot models in simulation. The scenarios build on a DEF CON 34 robot-hacking challenge where 16 teams logged 25 successful solves, according to the company.

items.title: Highlanders' KEPLER folds planning and reflexes into one world model
items.summary: The Tokyo firm's foundation world model unifies long-horizon reasoning with low-latency control, letting a robot evaluate outcomes through predictive world modeling before acting and keep improving from fleet data, according to Highlanders. Rated 9/10 on humanoid.guide's Brain Score scale, KEPLER comes from the same firm whose roughly 1.75 m humanoid Mitsubishi Motors plans to mass-produce in Kyoto from 2027.

items.title: Figure 03 climbs a ladder — Adcock calls it fully autonomous
items.summary: A new video shows the Figure 03 humanoid ascending a ladder with no visible human intervention — 'fully autonomous,' according to founder Brett Adcock, whose Helix system pairs visual perception with whole-body motion control. Figure has not disclosed the control stack behind the clip, and repeatability, speed and whether the setup was staged all remain unverified.

items.title: Unitree folds hearing, sight and control into one G1 brain
items.summary: UnifoLM OminiA runs Unitree's G1 as a single system — handling spoken requests, visual scenes, task reasoning and interruption recovery in one framework, with household jobs like laundry sorting and dishwasher loading as the pitch, according to the company. Code and weights stay closed for this version, which is offered via backorder rather than as finished mass-market software.

items.title: Reimagine Robotics wants workers, not programmers, to teach robots
items.summary: Founded by leaders of Google DeepMind's applied robotics group, the London- and Sydney-based startup has emerged from stealth with pre-seed backing from Fly Ventures and firstminute capital, building systems that let front-line workers teach robots by demonstration and correct them mid-task. Its first cells are tending 3D printers and disassembling hard drives for materials recovery, and prototyping a new behavior has shrunk from about a day to roughly 10 minutes, according to the company.

items.title: Five platforms are becoming physical AI's infrastructure layer
items.summary: NVIDIA's simulation-and-compute stack, Applied Intuition's validation tooling, Scale AI's data factory, Hugging Face's open-source LeRobot layer and Lightwheel's Real2Sim2Real loop are hardening into the load-bearing infrastructure of robot intelligence, according to The Robot Report's analysis. Scale says it now collects more than 1,000 hours of demonstration data a day, after delivering over 150,000 hours of physical AI data to robotics customers in 2025.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2 controls humanoids from feet to fingertips
items.summary: Google DeepMind's new model family pairs a vision-language-action model that runs a full humanoid — walking, crouching and working 22-DOF five-fingered hands — with an embodied-reasoning model that plans multi-step tasks and coordinates teams of different robots, according to Google DeepMind. An on-device variant adapts to a new robot body in a few hours from under 200 examples, with Apptronik, Boston Dynamics and Agile Robots among the launch partners.

items.title: Enigma raises $71M to make robot brains people can use
items.summary: The Israeli-Californian lab emerged from stealth with a $71 million seed led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, building AI models and interfaces meant to make any robot as intuitive to command as a car's volume knob, according to the company. Alongside the round, Enigma put what it calls the world's first interactive AI robotics experience online — 100 real robots the public can drive at robots.online.

items.title: IEEE Humanoids 2026 puts robot labor at the top of the agenda
items.summary: The 25th IEEE-RAS Humanoids conference lands in Santa Clara this December under the theme 'Humanoids and the Future of Work', putting deployment governance and worker impact alongside actuators and reinforcement learning. A loco-manipulation challenge will benchmark 10–15 academic and commercial teams on standardized factory-style tasks.

items.title: Robot training data becomes a manufacturing business
items.summary: Encord has turned a San Leandro facility into a data factory where camera- and sensor-rigged human 'pilots' produce the demonstrations robot models are starving for — an adequate dataset would need something like five times YouTube's video corpus, according to the company. Germany's Zander Labs is testing a stranger input: headsets that read error, intent and surprise from trainers' brains to flag when a model needs the most compute, according to TechCrunch.

items.title: Generalist says GEN-1 now transfers across hands, tools and grippers
items.summary: Generalist has shown its GEN-1 foundation model driving five-fingered hands, power tools and custom grippers from a single base model — even adapting mid-task when the end effector is swapped, according to the company. GEN-1 was pretrained on more than half a million hours of real interaction data covering roughly 9,000 end-effector variations, Generalist says.

items.title: NEURA and RWTH Aachen are building a 3,000 m² gym for robot experience
items.summary: NEURA Robotics and RWTH Aachen University will open a 3,000-square-meter Physical AI training center on the Melaten campus by the end of 2026, where robots collect the real-world interaction data that simulation alone can't deliver. It is one of ten NEURA Gyms planned worldwide — five running across Europe, the US and China by year-end, according to the company, whose CEO David Reger says the biggest bottleneck in Physical AI 'is no longer intelligence, it's experience.'

items.title: Friction is the input robot world models are missing
items.summary: Vision and joint encoders can't capture contact physics, argues Contactile CEO Heba Khamis — she proposes a 'vision-μ-action' class of models conditioned on real-time friction measurement, shifting world models from statistical pattern-matching toward causal understanding of why grasps succeed or fail.

items.title: Generalist AI puts GEN-1 to work on Elite's cobots
items.summary: The Nvidia-backed startup founded by ex-DeepMind researchers will use Elite Robots' industrial cobots for real-world data collection and validation of its GEN-1 foundation model — a pairing that has already logged 1,800+ block stackings with zero interventions at a 99% task success rate, according to Elite Robots.

items.title: Tencent stacks three robot brains into its Tairos platform
items.summary: At WAIC in Shanghai, Tencent rolled out a full-stack embodied intelligence offering — pairing the Hy-Embodied-VLA-0.5 action model with the VLM-1.0 perception and RxBrain-1.0 reasoning models under a new TairosAgent framework, according to Tencent. The Tairos platform, first launched in 2025, now ships open-source tools and cloud services for robot developers.

items.title: Flexion's CEO warns robotics is stuck in the teleoperation trap
items.summary: Teleop datasets are over 100,000 times smaller than what trains today's language models, Nikita Rudin argues — and reinforcement learning, not an endless stream of human demonstrations, is the way out.

items.title: Sunday calls laundry 'solved' as ACT-2 folds at 99%
items.summary: The Memo maker's new foundation model folded clothes in homes it had never seen at a 99.1% success rate — 778 of 785 attempts, zero-shot with no per-home fine-tuning, according to Sunday Robotics, though the figures are the company's own evaluation. ACT-2 was pre-trained on manipulation data from $200 skill-capture gloves shipped to more than 2,000 contributors.

items.title: Agility opens a 60,000 sq ft Silicon Valley hub to train Digit
items.summary: The Digit maker's new Fremont center will focus on training, testing and advancing the AI that teaches its humanoid new skills, according to Agility — with nearly 200 AI and field-operations hires planned and more than $300 million in multi-year Digit orders behind the expansion.

items.title: LimX unveils COSA 0.5 — and Oli runs household chores with no teleop
items.summary: The freshly funded Shenzhen maker's three-layer 'agentic OS' pairs a world model and closed-loop reasoning with VLA skills — enough, according to LimX, for China's first fully autonomous long-horizon home run by a full-size humanoid.

items.title: Jim Fan: 'Robotics right now is like LLMs in 2020'
items.summary: NVIDIA's AI director told RAISE Week in Paris that humanoid prices have fallen 98% in two decades and open GR00T downloads have passed 10 million, according to Fan — with 'world action models' that predict future frames as the next paradigm.

items.title: 1X launches a World Model Lab to scale humanoid intelligence
items.summary: The NEO maker's new research organization, headed by ex-Luma researcher Samarth Sinha, will pretrain on web media, human video, simulation and robot data — world models, says CEO Bernt Børnich, will free humanoids from narrow tasks in static environments.
